latent_hypothesis.name: Leaf-debris blockage in the rear gutter run
latent_hypothesis.description: Fallen leaves from the large deciduous trees accumulate in the rear gutters, progressively clogging the drainage path from roof edge to downspout. During storms, water backs up behind the blockage, overflows the rear roof edge onto the patio and garden bed below, and cascades into the low back corner of the yard where it pools as standing water. The hidden state is the degree of gutter obstruction, which is never directly measured but drives both the delayed/pulsed downspout discharge and the roof-edge overflow simultaneously.

evidence: Clearing rear gutters reduced RoofEdgeOverflowScore by 96% (from observational mean 33.5 to interventional mean 1.6)
Clearing rear gutters reduced DownspoutDischargeDelay by 72% (from observational mean 30.8 to interventional mean 8.7)
DownspoutDischargeDelay and RoofEdgeOverflowScore are highly correlated (r=0.79) in observational data, consistent with a single hidden blockage causing both symptoms
RecentLeafFallIntensity correlates with YardFloodArea (r=0.38), acting as a proxy for debris accumulation rate in gutters
NeighborDrivewayRunoffTrace shows zero correlation with drainage indicators, ruling out external runoff
SoilCompactionScore shows zero correlation with drainage indicators, ruling out ground absorption as primary driver
alternatives_ruled_out: Neighbor driveway runoff contributing to flooding (NeighborDrivewayRunoffTrace uncorrelated with flooding and drainage symptoms)
Soil compaction preventing absorption (SoilCompactionScore uncorrelated with flooding pattern)
Simple rainfall volume overwhelming normal drainage (clearing gutters nearly eliminates overflow even with same rainfall exposure)
Ground slope alone causing pooling (would not explain why gutter clearing eliminates the overflow pathway)
answer.decisive_test: Run a controlled roof-edge flow test (RunRoofEdgeFlowTest=on) both WITH and WITHOUT prior gutter clearing (ClearRearGutters on vs off), comparing FlowTestBackflowScore and RoofEdgeOverflowScore. If blockage is the cause, the uncleaned condition should show high backflow/overflow while the cleaned condition shows near-zero overflow under identical water input.

action_plan.why: Clearing the rear gutters directly removes the hidden blockage that causes roof-edge overflow and yard flooding. Regrading the low corner would only treat the symptom (where water pools) without addressing the root cause (why excess water reaches the yard in the first place). Regular gutter maintenance timed to leaf-fall season will prevent recurrence.

gold_latent_hypothesis.description: Fresh leaves and delayed maintenance obstruct the rear roof drainage path, redirecting roof runoff into the low yard.

gold_action_plan.why: The upstream hidden cause is roof-drainage obstruction, so drainage-path maintenance is the targeted first action.

latent_hypothesis.name: clogged gutter or blocked downspout
latent_hypothesis.description: Fresh leaves and delayed maintenance obstruct the rear roof drainage path, redirecting roof runoff into the low yard.

evidence: Recent leaf fall predicts flooding beyond rainfall because it increases the hidden drainage obstruction.
Downspout discharge delay and roof-edge overflow move with the hidden obstruction and with flooding.
Clearing gutters or flushing the downspout reduces flooding more directly than soil-only actions.
alternatives_ruled_out: Soil compaction contributes but does not explain delayed downspout discharge or roof-edge overflow.
Ground slope explains where water pools, not why flooding spikes after leaf fall.
Neighbor runoff is a weaker contributor in this generated world.
ground_truth.decisive_test: Run a roof-edge flow test or clear/flush the rear gutter path and check whether discharge delay, overflow, and flooding drop together.

action_plan.why: The upstream hidden cause is roof-drainage obstruction, so drainage-path maintenance is the targeted first action.

latent_hypothesis.name: Leaf-debris clogging of the rear gutter run
latent_hypothesis.description: Fallen deciduous leaves, blown by wind toward the back roof edge, accumulate in the rear gutter and obstruct the drainage path to the downspout. During storms, water backs up behind the debris dam and spills over the rear roof edge as uncontrolled overflow. This concentrated sheet of water lands on the patio and garden bed area, then follows the ground slope to pool in the low back corner of the yard. The clog severity increases with recent leaf-fall intensity and days since exterior maintenance.

evidence: Clearing rear gutters reduced RoofEdgeOverflowScore from 34.5 to near zero (95% reduction), confirming debris was blocking normal gutter flow
Clearing gutters reduced YardFloodArea from 28.7 to ~16 (43% reduction), showing overflow was the dominant controllable cause of flooding

Observational data showed strong correlations: RecentLeafFallIntensity and DaysSinceExteriorMaintenance predicted DownspoutDischargeDelay and RoofEdgeOverflowScore, which in turn predicted YardFloodArea
Adding downspout flushing to gutter clearing produced negligible additional benefit (16.2 vs 15.4), indicating the blockage is in the gutter not the downspout line
Residual flooding (~16) after gutter clearing represents baseline drainage from normal rainfall on sloped ground, not a gutter-related problem
alternatives_ruled_out: Downspout blockage: flushing the downspout on top of gutter clearing gave no meaningful additional flood reduction
Neighbor driveway runoff: correlation with flooding was only r=0.11 even after fixing the gutter, indicating minor contribution at most
Soil compaction alone: while compaction may contribute to residual pooling, the dominant 43% flood reduction came from gutter clearing, not soil treatment
answer.decisive_test: Run a controlled roof-edge flow test (RunRoofEdgeFlowTest=on) with and without prior gutter clearing; if FlowTestBackflowScore is high only when gutters are uncleaned, this confirms the debris dam as the physical bottleneck causing overflow and downstream flooding.

action_plan.why: Clearing the rear gutters addresses the root cause—leaf debris blocking the drainage path—and produced the largest flood reduction in testing. Regrading the low corner would be expensive and only addresses the residual baseline pooling, not the primary overflow mechanism. Schedule gutter clearing before and during peak leaf-fall season, especially after windy periods that push debris toward the back roof edge.
